text: The double-dual map V → V** is a natural transformation, whereas the isomorphisms V ≅ V* for finite-dimensional V cannot be chosen naturally.
explanation: v ↦ (f ↦ f(v)) needs no choices and commutes with all linear maps, giving a natural transformation Id ⇒ (−)**. Any V ≅ V* depends on a basis or bilinear form, and no family of such isomorphisms is natural (V ↦ V* is contravariant). This example motivated Eilenberg and Mac Lane to invent category theory.
